reviews.cons: Sometimes can be not so user-friendly, I often get confused when orders don't want to "Process".

reviews.title: Fr finance
reviews.name: Jeff S.
reviews.pros: Work stations and scanning job orders was good
reviews.cons: Reporting and finance Reporting difficult and Ul was not good

reviews.title: Installation of ECi M1
reviews.name: Mark P.
reviews.pros: This ERP software is very intuitive and very flexible relative to the previous software from Made2Manage that my organization ran for the past 24 years. The input of transactions is straightforward with minimal training, and searching for almost any data is substantially easier.
reviews.cons: The only issue we've had any challenge with so far is with the conversion of our old Made2Manage data, which was an old FoxPro version into a pure SQL format. Some data came across easily, and some data didn't come across at all. We could have come up to speed running the new software much faster if we'd have been able to convert our M2M data in a more timely fashion.

reviews.title: Good UI overall experience
reviews.name: Carlos A.
reviews.pros: Easy for end user learning curve, browser native UI, highly customizable screen forms, standard accounting and finance processes
reviews.cons: Lacks some native business processes like sales contract agreement management, some flows might be slow for user experience with ERP desktop apps

reviews.title: Powerful All-in-One ERP with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Sonu P.
reviews.pros: NetSuite provides strong value by combining multiple business functions into one platform, reducing the need for separate tools. It offers good data management with real-time visibility and efficient invoicing features that streamline billing processes. The system becomes easy to use once familiar, with helpful dashboards and automation improving productivity. Additionally, built-in email communication and reliable customer support enhance overall user experience.
reviews.cons: NetSuite can be expensive, especially for small businesses, and some features require additional paid modules. The system has a learning curve, and the interface can feel outdated at times. Customer support may be slow without premium plans, and occasional bugs or performance issues can impact workflows. Customization and data management can also become complex without proper expertise.

reviews.title: Solid ERP but challenging to learn
reviews.name: E. D.
reviews.pros: Has a lot of flexibility. There are an enormous number of features and possibilities. It is well established so you know you can rely on core GL.
reviews.cons: There is so much you can do that it is difficult to learn everything. The documentation is terrible and most functionality is additional models they upsell.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Joseph L.
reviews.pros: Ease of use and everything in one place. NetSuite streamlines tasks and makes accessing real-time data simple and efficient.
reviews.cons: Limited support for issues. Long standing bugs, issues & enhancement requests are still not resolved to date. Cost of maintenance is too high.

reviews.title: My customer experience
reviews.name: Kevin Clark T.
reviews.pros: Easy to implement Easy to access Fast Comprehensive financials that offer more depth and breadth Multiple companies are supported in one instance
reviews.cons: A lot of advanced functions are locked behind modules where some functionality but not all are needed.

reviews.title: Good Software, but poor support
reviews.name: Heath B.
reviews.pros: NetSuite is very comprehensive and can be customized to any business. The annual cost is reasonable for the functionality that you get.
reviews.cons: NetSuite is a bit of a challenge in a manufacturing environment. It also attempts to be too comprehensive. There are just too many paths to do a single task. The use of roles complicates this even more. Different roles use different paths to do the same thing. When building reports, there are 5-10 different fields to choose from with the same name and many return no information. We were also charged extra for the addition of a few customizations that we needed. There are thousands of hours of training videos, but they all use the base software and many are out of date for the current user interface.

reviews.title: NetSuite as my personal best ERP system

reviews.pros: What I kike about NetSuite is how easily to store data and generate reports including how easy the integration from other application
reviews.cons: What I like the least about NetSuite in general is the pricing maybe as it a bit pricey compared to other ERPs

reviews.title: Very Excellent

reviews.pros: Like the most in the netsuite it is very intuitive and easy to use. You can easy navigate all th function.

The system worked efficiently, and its features were helpful in understanding business operations. Overall, I did not find any aspect that I would consider negative, and I am satisfied with my experience using NetSuite.

reviews.cons: Not about NetSuite but probably with the implementing partner who informed us about not being able to apply Vat Inc in our pricing.

It scales well as your business grows, provides real-time visibility across departments, and offers extensive customization options to match complex workflows.

This limitation reduces efficiency in space planning and order packing, requiring workarounds that add time and complexity to daily operations.

reviews.cons: Sometimes it’s a little slow. We have moments where things take a while to load like creating an order, records, etc

reviews.cons: It's a learning curve, but any platform we would have migrated to would have had a similar learning curve.

reviews.pros: Ease of use and data management has been made more efficient. You can login and work anywhere on earth
reviews.cons: Value for money. The licenses are expensive and it has been a considerable cost to the business. It is a concern.

reviews.title: Netsuite a good system for all
reviews.name: Czarina H.
reviews.pros: Netsuite is designed as an integrated system for ease of procurement and invoicing. Reconciliation is made easy and reporting is handy
reviews.cons: Sometimes it’s not easy to add fields in Customise for reporting purpose, eg adding job ID as a column. TPAR report picks up both Yes and No. Seems cannot list only those that are required for reporting… unless my colleague set up incorrectly. Also, the system seems running slow. Quite some buffering time waiting for next interface to come up.

reviews.title: Powerful but complex
reviews.name: Kevin S.
reviews.pros: After two years of using NetSuite Oracle, I can say it is a powerful all-in-one ERP that provides great value for money if your business fully leverages its breadth of features. Transaction management and invoicing are very robust once everything is properly configured, making it easier to centralize processes that would otherwise require several different tools. The system’s automation reduces manual work, I also appreciate that the platform is highly customizable, which means it can be adapted to different industries and business models.
reviews.cons: NetSuite comes with a steep learning curve, and its ease of use is not its strongest point. Navigating the system can feel overwhelming, especially for new users, and customization sometimes requires technical expertise that not every company has in-house. There's a lack of visual dashboards in oposition to similar ERPs and customer support answers sometimes are slower than expected

reviews.title: A Powerful ERP with a Learning Curve but Strong Business Impact
reviews.name: Praveen J.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. You can manage financials, inventory, orders, and customers without jumping between different systems, which makes processes much smoother and more reliable. I also like how flexible it is — you can customise fields, workflows, and reports to match real business needs. The real-time data is a big plus, especially when making decisions or troubleshooting issues. From an integration perspective, working with tools like Celigo makes it even more powerful. Overall, it saves time, reduces manual work, and gives better visibility across the entire business.
reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. Simple tasks sometimes require multiple steps, and the UI can feel outdated compared to modern platforms. Customisation, while powerful, often needs technical knowledge or developer support, which can slow things down. Reporting can also be tricky, as saved searches don’t always give exactly what you need without a lot of tweaking. Performance can be inconsistent at times, especially during large data loads. Overall, while it’s powerful, it does come with a learning curve and occasional frustration.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. Whether you’re a growing startup or a complex multi-entity organization, NetSuite adapts to the way your business operates rather than forcing you to change your processes to fit the software. You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.title: A Useful System with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Ogi S.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is that it keeps financial and operational data in one place, which makes it easier to follow transactions from start to finish. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.
reviews.pros: Flexibility for a custom solution allows organizations to tailor systems, processes, or products to meet their unique needs and goals. Instead of relying on rigid, one-size-fits-all approaches, a customizable solution adapts to changing requirements, integrates with existing tools, and scales alongside growth. This flexibility supports innovation by enabling teams to experiment, refine, and optimize without major constraints. It also improves efficiency, as features and workflows can be designed specifically for the task at hand. Ultimately, a flexible custom solution empowers businesses to stay competitive, respond quickly to market demands, and deliver more personalized experiences to their customers while maintaining long-term adaptability.
reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. Updates or requested improvements can take a significant amount of time to be implemented, which may slow down business processes or limit the ability to adapt quickly to changing requirements. This can be frustrating for users who rely on timely system improvements to increase efficiency or address specific operational needs. Reporting can be challenging to configure without technical knowledge, and performance may occasionally lag when handling large datasets.

reviews.pros: Netsuite is designed as an integrated system for ease of procurement and invoicing. Reconciliation is made easy and reporting is handy
reviews.cons: Sometimes it’s not easy to add fields in Customise for reporting purpose, eg adding job ID as a column. TPAR report picks up both Yes and No. Seems cannot list only those that are required for reporting… unless my colleague set up incorrectly. Also, the system seems running slow. Quite some buffering time waiting for next interface to come up.

reviews.title: Powerful but complex
reviews.name: Kevin S.
reviews.pros: After two years of using NetSuite Oracle, I can say it is a powerful all-in-one ERP that provides great value for money if your business fully leverages its breadth of features. Transaction management and invoicing are very robust once everything is properly configured, making it easier to centralize processes that would otherwise require several different tools. The system’s automation reduces manual work, I also appreciate that the platform is highly customizable, which means it can be adapted to different industries and business models.
reviews.cons: NetSuite comes with a steep learning curve, and its ease of use is not its strongest point. Navigating the system can feel overwhelming, especially for new users, and customization sometimes requires technical expertise that not every company has in-house. There's a lack of visual dashboards in oposition to similar ERPs and customer support answers sometimes are slower than expected

reviews.title: A Powerful ERP with a Learning Curve but Strong Business Impact
reviews.name: Praveen J.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. You can manage financials, inventory, orders, and customers without jumping between different systems, which makes processes much smoother and more reliable. I also like how flexible it is — you can customise fields, workflows, and reports to match real business needs. The real-time data is a big plus, especially when making decisions or troubleshooting issues. From an integration perspective, working with tools like Celigo makes it even more powerful. Overall, it saves time, reduces manual work, and gives better visibility across the entire business.
reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. Simple tasks sometimes require multiple steps, and the UI can feel outdated compared to modern platforms. Customisation, while powerful, often needs technical knowledge or developer support, which can slow things down. Reporting can also be tricky, as saved searches don’t always give exactly what you need without a lot of tweaking. Performance can be inconsistent at times, especially during large data loads. Overall, while it’s powerful, it does come with a learning curve and occasional frustration.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. Whether you’re a growing startup or a complex multi-entity organization, NetSuite adapts to the way your business operates rather than forcing you to change your processes to fit the software. You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.title: A Useful System with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Ogi S.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is that it keeps financial and operational data in one place, which makes it easier to follow transactions from start to finish. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.
reviews.pros: Flexibility for a custom solution allows organizations to tailor systems, processes, or products to meet their unique needs and goals. Instead of relying on rigid, one-size-fits-all approaches, a customizable solution adapts to changing requirements, integrates with existing tools, and scales alongside growth. This flexibility supports innovation by enabling teams to experiment, refine, and optimize without major constraints. It also improves efficiency, as features and workflows can be designed specifically for the task at hand. Ultimately, a flexible custom solution empowers businesses to stay competitive, respond quickly to market demands, and deliver more personalized experiences to their customers while maintaining long-term adaptability.
reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. Updates or requested improvements can take a significant amount of time to be implemented, which may slow down business processes or limit the ability to adapt quickly to changing requirements. This can be frustrating for users who rely on timely system improvements to increase efficiency or address specific operational needs. Reporting can be challenging to configure without technical knowledge, and performance may occasionally lag when handling large datasets.

Additionally, built-in email communication and reliable customer support enhance overall user experience.

Customization and data management can also become complex without proper expertise.

We were also charged extra for the addition of a few customizations that we needed. There are thousands of hours of training videos, but they all use the base software and many are out of date for the current user interface.

reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. You can manage financials, inventory, orders, and customers without jumping between different systems, which makes processes much smoother and more reliable. I also like how flexible it is — you can customise fields, workflows, and reports to match real business needs. The real-time data is a big plus, especially when making decisions or troubleshooting issues. From an integration perspective, working with tools like Celigo makes it even more powerful. Overall, it saves time, reduces manual work, and gives better visibility across the entire business.
reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. Simple tasks sometimes require multiple steps, and the UI can feel outdated compared to modern platforms. Customisation, while powerful, often needs technical knowledge or developer support, which can slow things down. Reporting can also be tricky, as saved searches don’t always give exactly what you need without a lot of tweaking. Performance can be inconsistent at times, especially during large data loads. Overall, while it’s powerful, it does come with a learning curve and occasional frustration.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. Whether you’re a growing startup or a complex multi-entity organization, NetSuite adapts to the way your business operates rather than forcing you to change your processes to fit the software. You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.title: A Useful System with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Ogi S.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is that it keeps financial and operational data in one place, which makes it easier to follow transactions from start to finish. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.
reviews.pros: Flexibility for a custom solution allows organizations to tailor systems, processes, or products to meet their unique needs and goals. Instead of relying on rigid, one-size-fits-all approaches, a customizable solution adapts to changing requirements, integrates with existing tools, and scales alongside growth. This flexibility supports innovation by enabling teams to experiment, refine, and optimize without major constraints. It also improves efficiency, as features and workflows can be designed specifically for the task at hand. Ultimately, a flexible custom solution empowers businesses to stay competitive, respond quickly to market demands, and deliver more personalized experiences to their customers while maintaining long-term adaptability.
reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. Updates or requested improvements can take a significant amount of time to be implemented, which may slow down business processes or limit the ability to adapt quickly to changing requirements. This can be frustrating for users who rely on timely system improvements to increase efficiency or address specific operational needs. Reporting can be challenging to configure without technical knowledge, and performance may occasionally lag when handling large datasets.

The system becomes easy to use once familiar, with helpful dashboards and automation improving productivity. Additionally, built-in email communication and reliable customer support enhance overall user experience.
reviews.cons: NetSuite can be expensive, especially for small businesses, and some features require additional paid modules. The system has a learning curve, and the interface can feel outdated at times. Customer support may be slow without premium plans, and occasional bugs or performance issues can impact workflows. Customization and data management can also become complex without proper expertise.

reviews.cons: NetSuite is a bit of a challenge in a manufacturing environment. It also attempts to be too comprehensive. There are just too many paths to do a single task. There are thousands of hours of training videos, but they all use the base software and many are out of date for the current user interface.

You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.title: A Useful System with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Ogi S.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is that it keeps financial and operational data in one place, which makes it easier to follow transactions from start to finish. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.

reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.
reviews.pros: Flexibility for a custom solution allows organizations to tailor systems, processes, or products to meet their unique needs and goals. Instead of relying on rigid, one-size-fits-all approaches, a customizable solution adapts to changing requirements, integrates with existing tools, and scales alongside growth. This flexibility supports innovation by enabling teams to experiment, refine, and optimize without major constraints. It also improves efficiency, as features and workflows can be designed specifically for the task at hand. Ultimately, a flexible custom solution empowers businesses to stay competitive, respond quickly to market demands, and deliver more personalized experiences to their customers while maintaining long-term adaptability.
reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. Updates or requested improvements can take a significant amount of time to be implemented, which may slow down business processes or limit the ability to adapt quickly to changing requirements. This can be frustrating for users who rely on timely system improvements to increase efficiency or address specific operational needs. Reporting can be challenging to configure without technical knowledge, and performance may occasionally lag when handling large datasets.

reviews.title: Powerful but complex
reviews.name: Kevin S.
reviews.pros: After two years of using NetSuite Oracle, I can say it is a powerful all-in-one ERP that provides great value for money if your business fully leverages its breadth of features. Transaction management and invoicing are very robust once everything is properly configured, making it easier to centralize processes that would otherwise require several different tools. The system’s automation reduces manual work, I also appreciate that the platform is highly customizable, which means it can be adapted to different industries and business models.
reviews.cons: NetSuite comes with a steep learning curve, and its ease of use is not its strongest point. Navigating the system can feel overwhelming, especially for new users, and customization sometimes requires technical expertise that not every company has in-house. There's a lack of visual dashboards in oposition to similar ERPs and customer support answers sometimes are slower than expected

reviews.title: A Powerful ERP with a Learning Curve but Strong Business Impact
reviews.name: Praveen J.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. You can manage financials, inventory, orders, and customers without jumping between different systems, which makes processes much smoother and more reliable. I also like how flexible it is — you can customise fields, workflows, and reports to match real business needs. The real-time data is a big plus, especially when making decisions or troubleshooting issues. From an integration perspective, working with tools like Celigo makes it even more powerful. Overall, it saves time, reduces manual work, and gives better visibility across the entire business.
reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. Simple tasks sometimes require multiple steps, and the UI can feel outdated compared to modern platforms. Customisation, while powerful, often needs technical knowledge or developer support, which can slow things down. Reporting can also be tricky, as saved searches don’t always give exactly what you need without a lot of tweaking. Performance can be inconsistent at times, especially during large data loads. Overall, while it’s powerful, it does come with a learning curve and occasional frustration.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. Whether you’re a growing startup or a complex multi-entity organization, NetSuite adapts to the way your business operates rather than forcing you to change your processes to fit the software. You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.name: Praveen J.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful but complex
reviews.name: Kevin S.
reviews.pros: After two years of using NetSuite Oracle, I can say it is a powerful all-in-one ERP that provides great value for money if your business fully leverages its breadth of features. Transaction management and invoicing are very robust once everything is properly configured, making it easier to centralize processes that would otherwise require several different tools. The system’s automation reduces manual work, I also appreciate that the platform is highly customizable, which means it can be adapted to different industries and business models.
reviews.cons: NetSuite comes with a steep learning curve, and its ease of use is not its strongest point. Navigating the system can feel overwhelming, especially for new users, and customization sometimes requires technical expertise that not every company has in-house. There's a lack of visual dashboards in oposition to similar ERPs and customer support answers sometimes are slower than expected

reviews.title: A Powerful ERP with a Learning Curve but Strong Business Impact
reviews.name: Praveen J.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. You can manage financials, inventory, orders, and customers without jumping between different systems, which makes processes much smoother and more reliable. I also like how flexible it is — you can customise fields, workflows, and reports to match real business needs. The real-time data is a big plus, especially when making decisions or troubleshooting issues. From an integration perspective, working with tools like Celigo makes it even more powerful. Overall, it saves time, reduces manual work, and gives better visibility across the entire business.
reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. Simple tasks sometimes require multiple steps, and the UI can feel outdated compared to modern platforms. Customisation, while powerful, often needs technical knowledge or developer support, which can slow things down. Reporting can also be tricky, as saved searches don’t always give exactly what you need without a lot of tweaking. Performance can be inconsistent at times, especially during large data loads. Overall, while it’s powerful, it does come with a learning curve and occasional frustration.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. Whether you’re a growing startup or a complex multi-entity organization, NetSuite adapts to the way your business operates rather than forcing you to change your processes to fit the software. You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.title: A Useful System with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Ogi S.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is that it keeps financial and operational data in one place, which makes it easier to follow transactions from start to finish. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.
reviews.pros: Flexibility for a custom solution allows organizations to tailor systems, processes, or products to meet their unique needs and goals. Instead of relying on rigid, one-size-fits-all approaches, a customizable solution adapts to changing requirements, integrates with existing tools, and scales alongside growth. This flexibility supports innovation by enabling teams to experiment, refine, and optimize without major constraints. It also improves efficiency, as features and workflows can be designed specifically for the task at hand. Ultimately, a flexible custom solution empowers businesses to stay competitive, respond quickly to market demands, and deliver more personalized experiences to their customers while maintaining long-term adaptability.
reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. Updates or requested improvements can take a significant amount of time to be implemented, which may slow down business processes or limit the ability to adapt quickly to changing requirements. This can be frustrating for users who rely on timely system improvements to increase efficiency or address specific operational needs. Reporting can be challenging to configure without technical knowledge, and performance may occasionally lag when handling large datasets.

There's a lack of visual dashboards in oposition to similar ERPs and customer support answers sometimes are slower than expected

reviews.title: A Powerful ERP with a Learning Curve but Strong Business Impact
reviews.name: Praveen J.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. You can manage financials, inventory, orders, and customers without jumping between different systems, which makes processes much smoother and more reliable. I also like how flexible it is — you can customise fields, workflows, and reports to match real business needs. The real-time data is a big plus, especially when making decisions or troubleshooting issues. From an integration perspective, working with tools like Celigo makes it even more powerful. Overall, it saves time, reduces manual work, and gives better visibility across the entire business.
reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. Simple tasks sometimes require multiple steps, and the UI can feel outdated compared to modern platforms. Customisation, while powerful, often needs technical knowledge or developer support, which can slow things down. Reporting can also be tricky, as saved searches don’t always give exactly what you need without a lot of tweaking. Performance can be inconsistent at times, especially during large data loads. Overall, while it’s powerful, it does come with a learning curve and occasional frustration.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. Whether you’re a growing startup or a complex multi-entity organization, NetSuite adapts to the way your business operates rather than forcing you to change your processes to fit the software. You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.title: A Useful System with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Ogi S.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is that it keeps financial and operational data in one place, which makes it easier to follow transactions from start to finish. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.
reviews.pros: Flexibility for a custom solution allows organizations to tailor systems, processes, or products to meet their unique needs and goals. Instead of relying on rigid, one-size-fits-all approaches, a customizable solution adapts to changing requirements, integrates with existing tools, and scales alongside growth. This flexibility supports innovation by enabling teams to experiment, refine, and optimize without major constraints. It also improves efficiency, as features and workflows can be designed specifically for the task at hand. Ultimately, a flexible custom solution empowers businesses to stay competitive, respond quickly to market demands, and deliver more personalized experiences to their customers while maintaining long-term adaptability.
reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. Updates or requested improvements can take a significant amount of time to be implemented, which may slow down business processes or limit the ability to adapt quickly to changing requirements. This can be frustrating for users who rely on timely system improvements to increase efficiency or address specific operational needs. Reporting can be challenging to configure without technical knowledge, and performance may occasionally lag when handling large datasets.

reviews.title: Powerful but complex
reviews.name: Kevin S.
reviews.pros: After two years of using NetSuite Oracle, I can say it is a powerful all-in-one ERP that provides great value for money if your business fully leverages its breadth of features. Transaction management and invoicing are very robust once everything is properly configured, making it easier to centralize processes that would otherwise require several different tools. The system’s automation reduces manual work, I also appreciate that the platform is highly customizable, which means it can be adapted to different industries and business models.
reviews.cons: NetSuite comes with a steep learning curve, and its ease of use is not its strongest point. Navigating the system can feel overwhelming, especially for new users, and customization sometimes requires technical expertise that not every company has in-house. There's a lack of visual dashboards in oposition to similar ERPs and customer support answers sometimes are slower than expected

reviews.title: A Powerful ERP with a Learning Curve but Strong Business Impact
reviews.name: Praveen J.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. You can manage financials, inventory, orders, and customers without jumping between different systems, which makes processes much smoother and more reliable. I also like how flexible it is — you can customise fields, workflows, and reports to match real business needs. The real-time data is a big plus, especially when making decisions or troubleshooting issues. From an integration perspective, working with tools like Celigo makes it even more powerful. Overall, it saves time, reduces manual work, and gives better visibility across the entire business.
reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. Simple tasks sometimes require multiple steps, and the UI can feel outdated compared to modern platforms. Customisation, while powerful, often needs technical knowledge or developer support, which can slow things down. Reporting can also be tricky, as saved searches don’t always give exactly what you need without a lot of tweaking. Performance can be inconsistent at times, especially during large data loads. Overall, while it’s powerful, it does come with a learning curve and occasional frustration.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. Whether you’re a growing startup or a complex multi-entity organization, NetSuite adapts to the way your business operates rather than forcing you to change your processes to fit the software. You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.title: A Useful System with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Ogi S.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is that it keeps financial and operational data in one place, which makes it easier to follow transactions from start to finish. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.
reviews.pros: Flexibility for a custom solution allows organizations to tailor systems, processes, or products to meet their unique needs and goals. Instead of relying on rigid, one-size-fits-all approaches, a customizable solution adapts to changing requirements, integrates with existing tools, and scales alongside growth. This flexibility supports innovation by enabling teams to experiment, refine, and optimize without major constraints. It also improves efficiency, as features and workflows can be designed specifically for the task at hand. Ultimately, a flexible custom solution empowers businesses to stay competitive, respond quickly to market demands, and deliver more personalized experiences to their customers while maintaining long-term adaptability.
reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. Updates or requested improvements can take a significant amount of time to be implemented, which may slow down business processes or limit the ability to adapt quickly to changing requirements. This can be frustrating for users who rely on timely system improvements to increase efficiency or address specific operational needs. Reporting can be challenging to configure without technical knowledge, and performance may occasionally lag when handling large datasets.

There's a lack of visual dashboards in oposition to similar ERPs and customer support answers sometimes are slower than expected

reviews.title: A Powerful ERP with a Learning Curve but Strong Business Impact
reviews.name: Praveen J.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. You can manage financials, inventory, orders, and customers without jumping between different systems, which makes processes much smoother and more reliable. I also like how flexible it is — you can customise fields, workflows, and reports to match real business needs. The real-time data is a big plus, especially when making decisions or troubleshooting issues. From an integration perspective, working with tools like Celigo makes it even more powerful. Overall, it saves time, reduces manual work, and gives better visibility across the entire business.
reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. Simple tasks sometimes require multiple steps, and the UI can feel outdated compared to modern platforms. Customisation, while powerful, often needs technical knowledge or developer support, which can slow things down. Reporting can also be tricky, as saved searches don’t always give exactly what you need without a lot of tweaking. Performance can be inconsistent at times, especially during large data loads. Overall, while it’s powerful, it does come with a learning curve and occasional frustration.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. Whether you’re a growing startup or a complex multi-entity organization, NetSuite adapts to the way your business operates rather than forcing you to change your processes to fit the software. You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.title: A Useful System with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Ogi S.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is that it keeps financial and operational data in one place, which makes it easier to follow transactions from start to finish. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.
reviews.pros: Flexibility for a custom solution allows organizations to tailor systems, processes, or products to meet their unique needs and goals. Instead of relying on rigid, one-size-fits-all approaches, a customizable solution adapts to changing requirements, integrates with existing tools, and scales alongside growth. This flexibility supports innovation by enabling teams to experiment, refine, and optimize without major constraints. It also improves efficiency, as features and workflows can be designed specifically for the task at hand. Ultimately, a flexible custom solution empowers businesses to stay competitive, respond quickly to market demands, and deliver more personalized experiences to their customers while maintaining long-term adaptability.
reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. Updates or requested improvements can take a significant amount of time to be implemented, which may slow down business processes or limit the ability to adapt quickly to changing requirements. This can be frustrating for users who rely on timely system improvements to increase efficiency or address specific operational needs. Reporting can be challenging to configure without technical knowledge, and performance may occasionally lag when handling large datasets.

reviews.title: Powerful but complex
reviews.name: Kevin S.
reviews.pros: After two years of using NetSuite Oracle, I can say it is a powerful all-in-one ERP that provides great value for money if your business fully leverages its breadth of features. Transaction management and invoicing are very robust once everything is properly configured, making it easier to centralize processes that would otherwise require several different tools. The system’s automation reduces manual work, I also appreciate that the platform is highly customizable, which means it can be adapted to different industries and business models.
reviews.cons: NetSuite comes with a steep learning curve, and its ease of use is not its strongest point. Navigating the system can feel overwhelming, especially for new users, and customization sometimes requires technical expertise that not every company has in-house. There's a lack of visual dashboards in oposition to similar ERPs and customer support answers sometimes are slower than expected

reviews.title: A Powerful ERP with a Learning Curve but Strong Business Impact
reviews.name: Praveen J.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. You can manage financials, inventory, orders, and customers without jumping between different systems, which makes processes much smoother and more reliable. I also like how flexible it is — you can customise fields, workflows, and reports to match real business needs. The real-time data is a big plus, especially when making decisions or troubleshooting issues. From an integration perspective, working with tools like Celigo makes it even more powerful. Overall, it saves time, reduces manual work, and gives better visibility across the entire business.
reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. Simple tasks sometimes require multiple steps, and the UI can feel outdated compared to modern platforms. Customisation, while powerful, often needs technical knowledge or developer support, which can slow things down. Reporting can also be tricky, as saved searches don’t always give exactly what you need without a lot of tweaking. Performance can be inconsistent at times, especially during large data loads. Overall, while it’s powerful, it does come with a learning curve and occasional frustration.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. Whether you’re a growing startup or a complex multi-entity organization, NetSuite adapts to the way your business operates rather than forcing you to change your processes to fit the software. You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.title: A Useful System with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Ogi S.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is that it keeps financial and operational data in one place, which makes it easier to follow transactions from start to finish. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.
reviews.pros: Flexibility for a custom solution allows organizations to tailor systems, processes, or products to meet their unique needs and goals. Instead of relying on rigid, one-size-fits-all approaches, a customizable solution adapts to changing requirements, integrates with existing tools, and scales alongside growth. This flexibility supports innovation by enabling teams to experiment, refine, and optimize without major constraints. It also improves efficiency, as features and workflows can be designed specifically for the task at hand. Ultimately, a flexible custom solution empowers businesses to stay competitive, respond quickly to market demands, and deliver more personalized experiences to their customers while maintaining long-term adaptability.
reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. Updates or requested improvements can take a significant amount of time to be implemented, which may slow down business processes or limit the ability to adapt quickly to changing requirements. This can be frustrating for users who rely on timely system improvements to increase efficiency or address specific operational needs. Reporting can be challenging to configure without technical knowledge, and performance may occasionally lag when handling large datasets.

reviews.title: Powerful but complex
reviews.name: Kevin S.
reviews.pros: After two years of using NetSuite Oracle, I can say it is a powerful all-in-one ERP that provides great value for money if your business fully leverages its breadth of features. Transaction management and invoicing are very robust once everything is properly configured, making it easier to centralize processes that would otherwise require several different tools. The system’s automation reduces manual work, I also appreciate that the platform is highly customizable, which means it can be adapted to different industries and business models.
reviews.cons: NetSuite comes with a steep learning curve, and its ease of use is not its strongest point. Navigating the system can feel overwhelming, especially for new users, and customization sometimes requires technical expertise that not every company has in-house. There's a lack of visual dashboards in oposition to similar ERPs and customer support answers sometimes are slower than expected

reviews.title: A Powerful ERP with a Learning Curve but Strong Business Impact
reviews.name: Praveen J.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is how everything is connected in one place. You can manage financials, inventory, orders, and customers without jumping between different systems, which makes processes much smoother and more reliable. I also like how flexible it is — you can customise fields, workflows, and reports to match real business needs. The real-time data is a big plus, especially when making decisions or troubleshooting issues. From an integration perspective, working with tools like Celigo makes it even more powerful. Overall, it saves time, reduces manual work, and gives better visibility across the entire business.
reviews.cons: What I like least about NetSuite is that it can feel quite complex and not very user-friendly, especially for new users. Simple tasks sometimes require multiple steps, and the UI can feel outdated compared to modern platforms. Customisation, while powerful, often needs technical knowledge or developer support, which can slow things down. Reporting can also be tricky, as saved searches don’t always give exactly what you need without a lot of tweaking. Performance can be inconsistent at times, especially during large data loads. Overall, while it’s powerful, it does come with a learning curve and occasional frustration.

reviews.title: NetSuite Review
reviews.name: Dirk C.
reviews.pros: What I love most about NetSuite is the flexibility of the system. Whether you’re a growing startup or a complex multi-entity organization, NetSuite adapts to the way your business operates rather than forcing you to change your processes to fit the software. You can customize workflows, dashboards, and reports to match your specific needs, and as your business evolves, the platform scales right along with it. The ability to add modules — from financials and inventory to EPM and CRM — means you’re never locked into a one-size-fits-all solution. That kind of flexibility is rare in an ERP system, and it’s what makes NetSuite a long-term investment rather than just a short-term fix.
reviews.cons: One of my biggest frustrations with NetSuite is the slow performance. At times, the system can feel sluggish, particularly when running complex reports, loading large datasets, or navigating between modules. What should be a quick task can sometimes turn into a waiting game, which interrupts workflow and reduces overall productivity. During peak usage periods, the lag becomes even more noticeable, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently under time pressure — especially during month-end close or busy operational periods. While NetSuite is a powerful cloud-based platform, the performance doesn’t always reflect that power in day-to-day use. For a system that businesses rely on as their single source of truth, faster and more consistent response times would make a significant difference in the overall user experience.

reviews.title: A Useful System with a Learning Curve
reviews.name: Ogi S.
reviews.pros: What I like most about NetSuite is that it keeps financial and operational data in one place, which makes it easier to follow transactions from start to finish. I can see how a bill links to a purchase order and flows through to the general ledger without jumping between systems. Saved searches are also very helpful. I use them to track items like open bills, payment status, and exceptions. Once set up, they reduce the need to manually check multiple screens. I also find the structure across AP, purchasing, and GL practical for day-to-day work. It provides a consistent way to record transactions and makes month-end tasks more manageable. Overall, it helps keep processes organised and easier to review.
reviews.cons: One of the main challenges I’ve found with NetSuite is that some processes are not very intuitive, especially for new users. It can take time to understand where to find certain functions or how different records link together. The user interface can also feel a bit outdated, and navigating between screens sometimes requires more clicks than expected. This can slow down day-to-day tasks, particularly when handling high volumes. I’ve also noticed that certain actions, like correcting transactions or managing errors, are not always straightforward and may require workarounds or deeper system knowledge.

reviews.title: Powerful and Scalable ERP with a Steep Learning Curve
reviews.name: Rizwan K.
reviews.pros: Flexibility for a custom solution allows organizations to tailor systems, processes, or products to meet their unique needs and goals. Instead of relying on rigid, one-size-fits-all approaches, a customizable solution adapts to changing requirements, integrates with existing tools, and scales alongside growth. This flexibility supports innovation by enabling teams to experiment, refine, and optimize without major constraints. It also improves efficiency, as features and workflows can be designed specifically for the task at hand. Ultimately, a flexible custom solution empowers businesses to stay competitive, respond quickly to market demands, and deliver more personalized experiences to their customers while maintaining long-term adaptability.
reviews.cons: One of the main drawbacks is the delay in adding enhancements and new features. Updates or requested improvements can take a significant amount of time to be implemented, which may slow down business processes or limit the ability to adapt quickly to changing requirements. This can be frustrating for users who rely on timely system improvements to increase efficiency or address specific operational needs. Reporting can be challenging to configure without technical knowledge, and performance may occasionally lag when handling large datasets.
