reviews.pros: I have used Oracle to initiate and post journal entries, run GL and generate reports. It's easy to use and makes searching for journal entries, uploading, reviewing, posting very simple.
reviews.cons: There isn't anything I don't like about Oracle.

reviews.title: Makes payroll hassle-free!
reviews.name: Lori C.
reviews.pros: The fact you can upload time in various ways to this platform is incredibly helpful. We would accept time via the platform feed, fax, email, etc. This is crucial when dealing with timekeeping methods from various clients.
reviews.cons: I would love for there to be a communication system built in, perhaps notes or something of this nature. And for those to be tied to the payroll record.

reviews.title: Not intuitive and difficult to navigate
reviews.name: Lizzy S.
reviews.pros: There are many different categories where you can find and store information about different accounts.
reviews.cons: Peoplesoft my be a fine software, but it should not be used for higher education administration. It is lacking in clarity, functionality and both administrative and student facing functionality. It's also hard to edit anything on this software.

reviews.title: Robust system for mid-size to large enterprises
reviews.name: Jamon H.
reviews.pros: Robust system that can accommodate extremely high transactional volume
reviews.cons: User interface lacks imagination, and is somewhat disconnected from normal business transaction flow

reviews.title: Oracle People Soft. Best Accounting Package to buy.
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: It is like all under one roof. we can manage and review financial aspects, analyze our inventory tracking, rate our suppliers and can manage them easily,etc. etc.
reviews.cons: Internet should be available all the times. Sometimes due to technical issues we can face serious problems.

reviews.title: Long-term human resource management systems
reviews.name: hedaia J.
reviews.pros: In terms of ERP and HRM, PeopleSoft is a top-notch solution. Employee data serve as the basis for this cloud-based application, which is used to manage numerous business requirements. Anyone can use it because it has a simple user interface. By using several IDs, you can search for an employee and get all the records they've kept while working for you in PeopleSoft. To put it succinctly, I admire Oracle systems because they place a high value on the long-term viability of the organization as a whole.
reviews.cons: In spite of the fact that this isn't always a bad thing, you must always stop working while technology specialists provide technical support, which is inconvenient at times. I also think the user interface's simplicity is outdated and needs to be updated, as it frequently bores me.

reviews.title: Clunky and Slow
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: You can add frequently used reports or screens to your My Favorites list for easy access. The Worklist functionality makes it easy to see what PTRs (Personnel Transaction Requests) are awaiting your action.
reviews.cons: PeopleSoft is clunky and slow. I spend so much of my day watching the blue loading icon cycle. The reports have long names that aren't very intuitive, e.g. Commit Accting Cross-Reference shows you what positions are currently assigned to a particular account. There are hundreds of different roles to be able to view, create, and approve different requests. The role titles and descriptions are confusing, and they aren't grouped by job function. Whenever you hire a new person, it's exhausting to figure out what roles they will need to perform their job.

reviews.title: PeopleSoft
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: There is a lot that can be done with this software. My current job requires us to use this software as well as the university where I am currently a student. Part of my job is to generate expense reports or fund equity reports as well as create and update vouchers through this software and so far it has been productive.
reviews.cons: When I generate reports, it takes about 3 minutes per report. I usually have to generate reports for multiple departments so in order to save time, I like to initiate the process for all of them so that I can multitask and save time. Unfortunately when I do that, the system gets confused and doesn't register when I pick a different department and ends up generating 2 of the same report. I think that is something that they can optimize better.

reviews.title: Very flexible system, easy to use
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: Easy to learn, easy to navigate system. Once you are comfortable with one version of People Soft, you can easily adopt to upgrades. It is almost impossible to post out of balance journal ( system protects itself). Account mapping is not complicated, but does require knowledge of People Soft and accounting itself ( like ability to do T accounts). I worked on People Soft in the very large and medium one, People Soft worked well in both companies
reviews.cons: Some variety of People Soft do not allow to run across different business units and this is quite painful for accounting group during month end close. Crystal reports could be very tricky and have a tendency to slow down at the inopportune moments.

reviews.title: Poorly designed
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: Not much. The financial portion was pretty limited but it made it sort of easy to understand without too much training.
reviews.cons: The HR product was godawful. Payroll Expense Transfers would take hours to complete bc costs would go to 2 decimals but percentages to 3, and the system would automatically round up to costs that actually weren’t there if the two were at odds. Sometimes this would happen I should say, and it wasn’t consistent. Total waste of time for something that shouldn’t happen.

reviews.title: ORACLE PEOPLESOFT
reviews.name: BRIDGETTE J.
reviews.pros: I have peoplesoft for many years. If you purchase everything you need when getting the program, you should not have any issues using. We use the software for AP, AR and payroll.
reviews.cons: This particular peoplesoft software we are using for the current State Agency I work for is the worse peoplesoft software I ever used. It has limitations, not user friendly, and difficult to fix without cost.

reviews.title: Very Hokey Program
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: You've probably used Peoplesoft at some point in your life; whether you went to University or used it at work for HR Systems - it does a lot and has a lot of abilities; but, the cost is enormous and it had a lot of problems from an end-user perspective.
reviews.cons: Constantly having to update the software because end users have issues. Very hokey in its execution Constantly requires JAVA updates?? Oracle charges a lot to keep it in service.

reviews.title: Solid product!
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: The system is not flashy but it gets the job done. I used it at the University I worked at to track students grades, classes, financial info, etc. Once you learn how to navigate the system (which isn't too difficult) you have access to a lot information quickly.
reviews.cons: There was a little bit of a learning curve as you get used to the system. However, once you understand the functionality, it's very useful.

reviews.title: Terrible interfacing, glitchy
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: I am required to use this software to interact with Legal Aid as a private lawyer. The only positive thing that I can say is that it is relatively simple in its interface.
reviews.cons: Navigation is absolutely terrible. If using the back button in browser, the session usually times out or glitches, requiring a fresh login. Navigation can be quite confusing and difficult.

reviews.title: Great for Large Organization
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: Easy to navigate, well organized, categorization works great, fast, many features available for large numbers of employees, possibility to designate different access for different employees.
reviews.cons: The interface looks rather primitive, and it might not be cost effective for smaller organizations.

reviews.title: Fairly seamless with training
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: It serves as an effective database for my company. Once trained on how to enter information and pull certain information out - metrics can be easy to review.
reviews.cons: End users don't necessarily have the ability to customize reporting. Special requests have to be made but that could be the way that my company has it configured.

reviews.title: Difficult implementation, but very robust
reviews.name: Felix P.
reviews.pros: Very robust tools and I like the data structure. From a vanilla implementation perspective, it's very clean as an HRIS system. The modules are straightforward and there is a lot of spec documentation available.
reviews.cons: Customization is a beast. A lot of testing involved an depending on the consultants you have, may be a pain to customize from vanilla Peoplesoft.

reviews.title: Great User Administration
reviews.name: Ryan S.
reviews.pros: My former organization used PeopleSoft to manage our student population. The software easily allowed us to track students through their life-cycles at the university. Additionally, we enjoyed the ability to track our alumni and keep a database of their current areas, using them for donations in the future.
reviews.cons: Despite having great features, this software is a little more challenging to learn. However, Oracle does provide some excellent training videos online and their conference gives an even more in-depth look at the product.

reviews.title: People Soft is a must have
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: It makes the job easier, you can obtain many different reports, forms and basically an all in one helper
reviews.cons: I love this product so much there is nothing I truly disliked

reviews.title: Good Product with Lots of Features But Difficult to Maintain
reviews.name: Jared H.
reviews.pros: I like how customizable the tool is to match whatever business process you have. It has strong reporting capabilities and can handle very complex process.
reviews.cons: With the customization we had to do lots of regression testing when new updates came out. Sometimes this broke our customization and required much more work.

reviews.title: PeopleSoft is a great HR tool
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: I like having 1 place to update personal details, review job titles and compensation, request PTO and submit requests such as gym or college expenses reimbursements.
reviews.cons: I can't really think of anything negative about PeopleSoft. It's easy to use and I wouldn't want it to change.

reviews.title: Good software with lots of reporting functions.
reviews.name: June B.
reviews.pros: Integrated with online applications well, great reporting options and easy export to Excel. Process is streamlined and easy to enter notes, add orders, customers, etc.
reviews.cons: Reporting is great but seems to be hard for many people to grasp as there are so many options to choose from when running a report. Does let you save reports but if you need to tweak, most people need a Subject Matter Expert to help them.

reviews.title: Difficult to learn at first but full of info
reviews.name: AnnaLisa S.
reviews.pros: This program has so much information in it once you learn it. After 4 years of using it, i am still amazed when i learn more. It's a love hate thing lol. It helps me to save favorites, then i don't have to remember so many paths.
reviews.cons: That there are so many paths to remember. And since the most recent update or so, it no longer shows the bread crumbs on top. So when i am training others, it's not possible to follow them (breadcrumbs).

reviews.title: Long-term human resource management systems
reviews.name: hedaia J.
reviews.pros: In terms of ERP and HRM, PeopleSoft is a top-notch solution. Employee data serve as the basis for this cloud-based application, which is used to manage numerous business requirements. Anyone can use it because it has a simple user interface. By using several IDs, you can search for an employee and get all the records they've kept while working for you in PeopleSoft. To put it succinctly, I admire Oracle systems because they place a high value on the long-term viability of the organization as a whole.
reviews.cons: In spite of the fact that this isn't always a bad thing, you must always stop working while technology specialists provide technical support, which is inconvenient at times. I also think the user interface's simplicity is outdated and needs to be updated, as it frequently bores me.

reviews.title: Clunky and Slow
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: You can add frequently used reports or screens to your My Favorites list for easy access. The Worklist functionality makes it easy to see what PTRs (Personnel Transaction Requests) are awaiting your action.
reviews.cons: PeopleSoft is clunky and slow. I spend so much of my day watching the blue loading icon cycle. The reports have long names that aren't very intuitive, e.g. Commit Accting Cross-Reference shows you what positions are currently assigned to a particular account. There are hundreds of different roles to be able to view, create, and approve different requests. The role titles and descriptions are confusing, and they aren't grouped by job function. Whenever you hire a new person, it's exhausting to figure out what roles they will need to perform their job.

reviews.title: PeopleSoft
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: There is a lot that can be done with this software. My current job requires us to use this software as well as the university where I am currently a student. Part of my job is to generate expense reports or fund equity reports as well as create and update vouchers through this software and so far it has been productive.
reviews.cons: When I generate reports, it takes about 3 minutes per report. I usually have to generate reports for multiple departments so in order to save time, I like to initiate the process for all of them so that I can multitask and save time. Unfortunately when I do that, the system gets confused and doesn't register when I pick a different department and ends up generating 2 of the same report. I think that is something that they can optimize better.

reviews.title: Very flexible system, easy to use
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: Easy to learn, easy to navigate system. Once you are comfortable with one version of People Soft, you can easily adopt to upgrades. It is almost impossible to post out of balance journal ( system protects itself). Account mapping is not complicated, but does require knowledge of People Soft and accounting itself ( like ability to do T accounts). I worked on People Soft in the very large and medium one, People Soft worked well in both companies
reviews.cons: Some variety of People Soft do not allow to run across different business units and this is quite painful for accounting group during month end close. Crystal reports could be very tricky and have a tendency to slow down at the inopportune moments.

reviews.title: Poorly designed

Sometimes this would happen I should say, and it wasn’t consistent. Total waste of time for something that shouldn’t happen.

Whenever you hire a new person, it's exhausting to figure out what roles they will need to perform their job.

reviews.name:

Reviewer
reviews.pros: There is a lot that can be done with this software. My current job requires us to use this software as well as the university where I am currently a student. Reviewer

reviews.cons: Some variety of People Soft do not allow to run across different business units and this is quite painful for accounting group during month end close. Crystal reports could be very tricky and have a tendency to slow down at the inopportune moments.

reviews.title: Poorly designed
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer

reviews.title: Very Hokey Program
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer

reviews.cons: Constantly having to update the software because end users have issues. Very hokey in its execution Constantly requires JAVA updates?? Oracle charges a lot to keep it in service.

reviews.title: Solid product!
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: The system is not flashy but it gets the job done. I used it at the University I worked at to track students grades, classes, financial info, etc. Once you learn how to navigate the system (which isn't too difficult) you have access to a lot information quickly.
reviews.cons: There was a little bit of a learning curve as you get used to the system. However, once you understand the functionality, it's very useful.

reviews.title: Terrible interfacing, glitchy
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: I am required to use this software to interact with Legal Aid as a private lawyer. The only positive thing that I can say is that it is relatively simple in its interface.
reviews.cons: Navigation is absolutely terrible. If using the back button in browser, the session usually times out or glitches, requiring a fresh login. Navigation can be quite confusing and difficult.

reviews.title: Great for Large Organization
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: Easy to navigate, well organized, categorization works great, fast, many features available for large numbers of employees, possibility to designate different access for different employees.
reviews.cons: The interface looks rather primitive, and it might not be cost effective for smaller organizations.

reviews.title: Fairly seamless with training
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: It serves as an effective database for my company. Once trained on how to enter information and pull certain information out - metrics can be easy to review.
reviews.cons: End users don't necessarily have the ability to customize reporting. Special requests have to be made but that could be the way that my company has it configured.

reviews.title: Difficult implementation, but very robust
reviews.name: Felix P.
reviews.pros: Very robust tools and I like the data structure. From a vanilla implementation perspective, it's very clean as an HRIS system. The modules are straightforward and there is a lot of spec documentation available.
reviews.cons: Customization is a beast. A lot of testing involved an depending on the consultants you have, may be a pain to customize from vanilla Peoplesoft.

reviews.title: Great User Administration
reviews.name: Ryan S.
reviews.pros: My former organization used PeopleSoft to manage our student population. The software easily allowed us to track students through their life-cycles at the university. Additionally, we enjoyed the ability to track our alumni and keep a database of their current areas, using them for donations in the future.
reviews.cons: Despite having great features, this software is a little more challenging to learn. However, Oracle does provide some excellent training videos online and their conference gives an even more in-depth look at the product.

reviews.title: People Soft is a must have
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: It makes the job easier, you can obtain many different reports, forms and basically an all in one helper
reviews.cons: I love this product so much there is nothing I truly disliked

reviews.title: Good Product with Lots of Features But Difficult to Maintain
reviews.name: Jared H.
reviews.pros: I like how customizable the tool is to match whatever business process you have. It has strong reporting capabilities and can handle very complex process.
reviews.cons: With the customization we had to do lots of regression testing when new updates came out. Sometimes this broke our customization and required much more work.

reviews.title: PeopleSoft is a great HR tool
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: I like having 1 place to update personal details, review job titles and compensation, request PTO and submit requests such as gym or college expenses reimbursements.
reviews.cons: I can't really think of anything negative about PeopleSoft. It's easy to use and I wouldn't want it to change.

reviews.title: Good software with lots of reporting functions.
reviews.name: June B.
reviews.pros: Integrated with online applications well, great reporting options and easy export to Excel. Process is streamlined and easy to enter notes, add orders, customers, etc.
reviews.cons: Reporting is great but seems to be hard for many people to grasp as there are so many options to choose from when running a report. Does let you save reports but if you need to tweak, most people need a Subject Matter Expert to help them.

reviews.title: Difficult to learn at first but full of info
reviews.name: AnnaLisa S.
reviews.pros: This program has so much information in it once you learn it. After 4 years of using it, i am still amazed when i learn more. It's a love hate thing lol. It helps me to save favorites, then i don't have to remember so many paths.
reviews.cons: That there are so many paths to remember. And since the most recent update or so, it no longer shows the bread crumbs on top. So when i am training others, it's not possible to follow them (breadcrumbs).

reviews.title: Decent product by a leading provider
reviews.name: Sabrina Y.
reviews.pros: One of the main features I love about this product is the development of reports and queries. It also allows reports to be exported into various formats as well.
reviews.cons: Some of the processes within the program are redundant. Requesting information can be a bit inefficient because the program requests various steps to produce one report or functionality within the system.

reviews.title: Good holistic HRIS
reviews.name: Matt M.
reviews.pros: The ability to manage all HR needs - compensation, performance, reporting, HRIS, etc. It was a very powerful tool as well and had lots of ability to create custom fields for extensive reporting capabilities.
reviews.cons: The interface, especially the reporting query portal, was difficult to learn and navigate.

reviews.title: Oracle Review
reviews.name: Lena P.
reviews.pros: I have used Oracle to initiate and post journal entries, run GL and generate reports. It's easy to use and makes searching for journal entries, uploading, reviewing, posting very simple.
reviews.cons: There isn't anything I don't like about Oracle.

reviews.title: Makes payroll hassle-free!

reviews.pros: The fact you can upload time in various ways to this platform is incredibly helpful. We would accept time via the platform feed, fax, email, etc. This is crucial when dealing with timekeeping methods from various clients.
reviews.cons: I would love for there to be a communication system built in, perhaps notes or something of this nature. And for those to be tied to the payroll record.

reviews.title: Not intuitive and difficult to navigate

reviews.pros: There are many different categories where you can find and store information about different accounts.

reviews.title: Difficult to learn at first but full of info
reviews.name: AnnaLisa S.
reviews.pros: This program has so much information in it once you learn it. After 4 years of using it, i am still amazed when i learn more. It's a love hate thing lol. It helps me to save favorites, then i don't have to remember so many paths.
reviews.cons: That there are so many paths to remember. And since the most recent update or so, it no longer shows the bread crumbs on top. So when i am training others, it's not possible to follow them (breadcrumbs).

reviews.title: Decent product by a leading provider
reviews.name: Sabrina Y.
reviews.pros: One of the main features I love about this product is the development of reports and queries. It also allows reports to be exported into various formats as well.
reviews.cons: Some of the processes within the program are redundant. Requesting information can be a bit inefficient because the program requests various steps to produce one report or functionality within the system.

reviews.title: Good holistic HRIS
reviews.name: Matt M.
reviews.pros: The ability to manage all HR needs - compensation, performance, reporting, HRIS, etc. It was a very powerful tool as well and had lots of ability to create custom fields for extensive reporting capabilities.
reviews.cons: The interface, especially the reporting query portal, was difficult to learn and navigate.

reviews.title: Oracle Review
reviews.name: Lena P.
reviews.pros: I have used Oracle to initiate and post journal entries, run GL and generate reports. It's easy to use and makes searching for journal entries, uploading, reviewing, posting very simple.
reviews.cons: There isn't anything I don't like about Oracle.

reviews.title: Makes payroll hassle-free!
reviews.name: Lori C.
reviews.pros: The fact you can upload time in various ways to this platform is incredibly helpful. We would accept time via the platform feed, fax, email, etc. This is crucial when dealing with timekeeping methods from various clients.
reviews.cons: I would love for there to be a communication system built in, perhaps notes or something of this nature. And for those to be tied to the payroll record.

reviews.title: Not intuitive and difficult to navigate
reviews.name: Lizzy S.
reviews.pros: There are many different categories where you can find and store information about different accounts.
reviews.cons: Peoplesoft my be a fine software, but it should not be used for higher education administration. It is lacking in clarity, functionality and both administrative and student facing functionality. It's also hard to edit anything on this software.

reviews.title: Robust system for mid-size to large enterprises
reviews.name: Jamon H.
reviews.pros: Robust system that can accommodate extremely high transactional volume
reviews.cons: User interface lacks imagination, and is somewhat disconnected from normal business transaction flow

reviews.title: Oracle People Soft. Best Accounting Package to buy.
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: It is like all under one roof. we can manage and review financial aspects, analyze our inventory tracking, rate our suppliers and can manage them easily,etc. etc.
reviews.cons: Internet should be available all the times. Sometimes due to technical issues we can face serious problems.

reviews.title: Long-term human resource management systems
reviews.name: hedaia J.
reviews.pros: In terms of ERP and HRM, PeopleSoft is a top-notch solution. Employee data serve as the basis for this cloud-based application, which is used to manage numerous business requirements. Anyone can use it because it has a simple user interface. By using several IDs, you can search for an employee and get all the records they've kept while working for you in PeopleSoft. To put it succinctly, I admire Oracle systems because they place a high value on the long-term viability of the organization as a whole.
reviews.cons: In spite of the fact that this isn't always a bad thing, you must always stop working while technology specialists provide technical support, which is inconvenient at times. I also think the user interface's simplicity is outdated and needs to be updated, as it frequently bores me.

reviews.title: Clunky and Slow
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: You can add frequently used reports or screens to your My Favorites list for easy access. The Worklist functionality makes it easy to see what PTRs (Personnel Transaction Requests) are awaiting your action.
reviews.cons: PeopleSoft is clunky and slow. I spend so much of my day watching the blue loading icon cycle. The reports have long names that aren't very intuitive, e.g. Commit Accting Cross-Reference shows you what positions are currently assigned to a particular account. There are hundreds of different roles to be able to view, create, and approve different requests. The role titles and descriptions are confusing, and they aren't grouped by job function. Whenever you hire a new person, it's exhausting to figure out what roles they will need to perform their job.

reviews.title: PeopleSoft
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: There is a lot that can be done with this software. My current job requires us to use this software as well as the university where I am currently a student. Part of my job is to generate expense reports or fund equity reports as well as create and update vouchers through this software and so far it has been productive.
reviews.cons: When I generate reports, it takes about 3 minutes per report. I usually have to generate reports for multiple departments so in order to save time, I like to initiate the process for all of them so that I can multitask and save time. Unfortunately when I do that, the system gets confused and doesn't register when I pick a different department and ends up generating 2 of the same report. I think that is something that they can optimize better.

reviews.title: Very flexible system, easy to use
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: Easy to learn, easy to navigate system. Once you are comfortable with one version of People Soft, you can easily adopt to upgrades. It is almost impossible to post out of balance journal ( system protects itself). Account mapping is not complicated, but does require knowledge of People Soft and accounting itself ( like ability to do T accounts). I worked on People Soft in the very large and medium one, People Soft worked well in both companies
reviews.cons: Some variety of People Soft do not allow to run across different business units and this is quite painful for accounting group during month end close. Crystal reports could be very tricky and have a tendency to slow down at the inopportune moments.

reviews.title: Poorly designed
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: Not much. The financial portion was pretty limited but it made it sort of easy to understand without too much training.
reviews.cons: The HR product was godawful. Payroll Expense Transfers would take hours to complete bc costs would go to 2 decimals but percentages to 3, and the system would automatically round up to costs that actually weren’t there if the two were at odds. Sometimes this would happen I should say, and it wasn’t consistent. Total waste of time for something that shouldn’t happen.

reviews.title: ORACLE PEOPLESOFT
reviews.name: BRIDGETTE J.
reviews.pros: I have peoplesoft for many years. If you purchase everything you need when getting the program, you should not have any issues using. We use the software for AP, AR and payroll.
reviews.cons: This particular peoplesoft software we are using for the current State Agency I work for is the worse peoplesoft software I ever used. It has limitations, not user friendly, and difficult to fix without cost.

reviews.title: Very Hokey Program
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: You've probably used Peoplesoft at some point in your life; whether you went to University or used it at work for HR Systems - it does a lot and has a lot of abilities; but, the cost is enormous and it had a lot of problems from an end-user perspective.
reviews.cons: Constantly having to update the software because end users have issues. Very hokey in its execution Constantly requires JAVA updates?? Oracle charges a lot to keep it in service.

reviews.title: Solid product!
reviews.name:
Verified
Reviewer
reviews.pros: The system is not flashy but it gets the job done. I used it at the University I worked at to track students grades, classes, financial info, etc. Once you learn how to navigate the system (which isn't too difficult) you have access to a lot information quickly.
reviews.cons: There was a little bit of a learning curve as you get used to the system. However, once you understand the functionality, it's very useful.

reviews.title: Terrible interfacing, glitchy

reviews.title: Great User Administration

Additionally, we enjoyed the ability to track our alumni and keep a database of their current areas, using them for donations in the future.

reviews.title: Powerful Accounting Software for Growing Businesses
reviews.name: Mailen G.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise has been a solid solution for managing accounting, invoicing, and business operations in one place. It offers powerful features for growing businesses, especially those that need advanced inventory tracking, detailed reporting, and multi-user access. While it has a learning curve at first, once everything is set up properly it becomes a very efficient system for daily operations. One of the biggest advantages of QuickBooks Enterprise is its robust invoicing and invoice management tools. Creating invoices is fast and customizable, and tracking payments is very straightforward. The reporting features are also excellent and provide valuable insights for financial management. The software handles large amounts of data smoothly compared to simpler accounting platforms. Customer support has generally been helpful when dealing with setup or technical questions, and there are many online resources and tutorials available. The mobile access is convenient for checking important information remotely, although some advanced features work better on desktop. In terms of value for money, it can be worth the investment for medium-sized or expanding businesses that need more advanced accounting capabilities than basic bookkeeping software offers.
reviews.cons: The software can feel overwhelming for new users because of the large number of features and settings. There is definitely a learning curve in the beginning. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. The mobile version is useful for basic tasks but does not provide the full desktop experience.

reviews.title: Easy to Use, Everything I need in one place
reviews.name: Zachary S.
reviews.pros: I like that my paychecks are linked up to my taxes on turbo tax so I don't have to do anything and it is all uploaded easily. I also like that you can do timesheets easily and there are different ways to do them. you can add just the hours or you can clock in and do hours.
reviews.cons: The interface can feel outdated and unintuitive at times, especially for new users. Some processes require multiple steps that could be streamlined, and performance can slow down with larger company files, which impacts overall efficiency.

reviews.title: Great Accounting tool!

reviews.cons: O s i not have something in particular that like least, what I really like about this tool is that we can find tutorials pretty easy to accomplish different task

reviews.title: Great system for medium sized company.

reviews.cons: Trying to get a hold of customer service can be difficult. When doung the annual update often you get locked out and need their support. Also when trying to provide new contacts they make you have to jump through hoops, even when the owner calls them to make the request. It would also be better if their were better search features on the autit report.

reviews.title: Solid Accounting

reviews.pros: The Feature that I like the most is that we can easily save each journal entry and there are no specific vouchers where we have to save entry instead we can save into one voucher simply debit and credit account.

reviews.title: The Most Functional Program

reviews.pros: QuickBooks provides an efficient way for us to store records, pay bills, enter invoices, and send bulk emails to vendors when needed. reviews.cons: I do not like the constant push to move to QuickBooks Online. I prefer the desktop version because it is simple and consistent, with each update making minimal changes. The online version relies heavily on internet connectivity and computer performance, which can introduce unnecessary complications and occasional disruptions.

reviews.pros: Powerful financial reporting tools with built-in templates and customization User-friendly interface that's easy to navigate even for non-accountants Advanced inventory management (especially with Platinum and Diamond editions) Multi-user access & role-based permissions ideal for medium-sized businesses Seamless integration with payroll, payments, and time-tracking tools
reviews.cons: The desktop-based architecture feels outdated compared to modern cloud ERP systems Integration with non-Intuit third-party tools is limited and sometimes buggy Customization options are not as flexible as cloud-based ERPs like Odoo or NetSuite Performance may lag with large data files or when accessed over network

reviews.title: Quickbooks for Billing

reviews.pros: Quickbooks really does what you need it to do. It is relatively easy to use (if you're OK with technology). It saves us SO much time. We do all our invoicing through QB. Their customer support is OK, but it is a good program at a good price. When there are bugs, they seem to be resolved quickly.
reviews.cons: I have noticed that they do a lot of updates. The most recent one changed everything around, which is fine, but I know some people have a hard time finding things. I also feel like they don't have enough information online, or it is really out of date. I feel like some customer service representatives don't understand the program.

reviews.cons: It didn't have the capabilities of an ERP software that you can customize to your own specifications. It is good for a smaller company.

reviews.title: Quickbooks Is the Bomb!
reviews.name: Sherrie G.
reviews.pros: Invoicing, monthly reporting and financial activities, ease of use and time saving features that make my life easier
reviews.cons: Sometimes it's difficult to get to the right customer service area. I have been put on hold many times just to be transferred to various other departments.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.cons: Some challenges with updates, specifically switching to single use and locking out users inadvertently. Multiuser should really be the standard for enterprise.

The most likely thing in quick books is we can manage quick books using laptop , phone etc, so as i can work while Iam travelling. The customer support is also a weak point for the software, as when the the transactions increase the quick books software becomes so slow.

reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a great tool to use for any business, especially with managing invoicing and communicating with customers.
reviews.cons: It can be a little tricky learning all the different functions but once you gain some experience it is quite easy to use.

It is especially useful for small business owners, freelancers, and service providers who want to stay organized without manually tracking everything.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise has been a solid solution for managing accounting, invoicing, and business operations in one place. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. The mobile version is useful for basic tasks but does not provide the full desktop experience.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

The reporting features are also excellent and provide valuable insights for financial management. The software handles large amounts of data smoothly compared to simpler accounting platforms. Customer support has generally been helpful when dealing with setup or technical questions, and there are many online resources and tutorials available. The mobile access is convenient for checking important information remotely, although some advanced features work better on desktop. In terms of value for money, it can be worth the investment for medium-sized or expanding businesses that need more advanced accounting capabilities than basic bookkeeping software offers.
reviews.cons: The software can feel overwhelming for new users because of the large number of features and settings. There is definitely a learning curve in the beginning. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. reviews.cons: It didn't have the capabilities of an ERP software that you can customize to your own specifications. It is good for a smaller company.

reviews.title: Quickbooks Is the Bomb!
reviews.name: Sherrie G.
reviews.pros: Invoicing, monthly reporting and financial activities, ease of use and time saving features that make my life easier
reviews.cons: Sometimes it's difficult to get to the right customer service area. I have been put on hold many times just to be transferred to various other departments.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.cons: Some challenges with updates, specifically switching to single use and locking out users inadvertently. Multiuser should really be the standard for enterprise.

reviews.cons: It didn't have the capabilities of an ERP software that you can customize to your own specifications. It is good for a smaller company.

reviews.cons: Sometimes it's difficult to get to the right customer service area. I have been put on hold many times just to be transferred to various other departments.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: Powerful Accounting Software for Growing Businesses
reviews.name: Mailen G.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise has been a solid solution for managing accounting, invoicing, and business operations in one place. It offers powerful features for growing businesses, especially those that need advanced inventory tracking, detailed reporting, and multi-user access. While it has a learning curve at first, once everything is set up properly it becomes a very efficient system for daily operations. One of the biggest advantages of QuickBooks Enterprise is its robust invoicing and invoice management tools. Creating invoices is fast and customizable, and tracking payments is very straightforward. The reporting features are also excellent and provide valuable insights for financial management. The software handles large amounts of data smoothly compared to simpler accounting platforms. Customer support has generally been helpful when dealing with setup or technical questions, and there are many online resources and tutorials available. The mobile access is convenient for checking important information remotely, although some advanced features work better on desktop. In terms of value for money, it can be worth the investment for medium-sized or expanding businesses that need more advanced accounting capabilities than basic bookkeeping software offers.
reviews.cons: The software can feel overwhelming for new users because of the large number of features and settings. There is definitely a learning curve in the beginning. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. The mobile version is useful for basic tasks but does not provide the full desktop experience.

reviews.cons: The desktop-based architecture feels outdated compared to modern cloud ERP systems Integration with non-Intuit third-party tools is limited and sometimes buggy Customization options are not as flexible as cloud-based ERPs like Odoo or NetSuite Performance may lag with large data files or when accessed over network

reviews.pros: Quickbooks really does what you need it to do. It is relatively easy to use (if you're OK with technology). It saves us SO much time. We do all our invoicing through QB. Their customer support is OK, but it is a good program at a good price. When there are bugs, they seem to be resolved quickly.
reviews.cons: I have noticed that they do a lot of updates. The most recent one changed everything around, which is fine, but I know some people have a hard time finding things. I also feel like they don't have enough information online, or it is really out of date. I feel like some customer service representatives don't understand the program.

reviews.title: Accounting Manager
reviews.name: Jeanne S.
reviews.pros: The inventory system is easy to use. We spent less time on training new employees because it was so user friendly and intuitive. I recently left the company where i used QB's Enterprise inventory and went to a new office that uses and ERP . The ERP isn't intuitive for staff and take a lot longer to learn how to use it.
reviews.cons: It didn't have the capabilities of an ERP software that you can customize to your own specifications. It is good for a smaller company.

reviews.title: Quickbooks Is the Bomb!
reviews.name: Sherrie G.
reviews.pros: Invoicing, monthly reporting and financial activities, ease of use and time saving features that make my life easier
reviews.cons: Sometimes it's difficult to get to the right customer service area. I have been put on hold many times just to be transferred to various other departments.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: Powerful Accounting Software for Growing Businesses
reviews.name: Mailen G.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise has been a solid solution for managing accounting, invoicing, and business operations in one place. It offers powerful features for growing businesses, especially those that need advanced inventory tracking, detailed reporting, and multi-user access. The reporting features are also excellent and provide valuable insights for financial management. The software handles large amounts of data smoothly compared to simpler accounting platforms. Customer support has generally been helpful when dealing with setup or technical questions, and there are many online resources and tutorials available. The mobile access is convenient for checking important information remotely, although some advanced features work better on desktop. In terms of value for money, it can be worth the investment for medium-sized or expanding businesses that need more advanced accounting capabilities than basic bookkeeping software offers.
reviews.cons: The software can feel overwhelming for new users because of the large number of features and settings. There is definitely a learning curve in the beginning. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. The mobile version is useful for basic tasks but does not provide the full desktop experience.

reviews.cons: The desktop-based architecture feels outdated compared to modern cloud ERP systems Integration with non-Intuit third-party tools is limited and sometimes buggy Customization options are not as flexible as cloud-based ERPs like Odoo or NetSuite Performance may lag with large data files or when accessed over network
