Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: Powerful Accounting Software for Growing Businesses
reviews.name: Mailen G.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise has been a solid solution for managing accounting, invoicing, and business operations in one place. It offers powerful features for growing businesses, especially those that need advanced inventory tracking, detailed reporting, and multi-user access. While it has a learning curve at first, once everything is set up properly it becomes a very efficient system for daily operations. One of the biggest advantages of QuickBooks Enterprise is its robust invoicing and invoice management tools. Creating invoices is fast and customizable, and tracking payments is very straightforward. The reporting features are also excellent and provide valuable insights for financial management. The software handles large amounts of data smoothly compared to simpler accounting platforms. Customer support has generally been helpful when dealing with setup or technical questions, and there are many online resources and tutorials available. The mobile access is convenient for checking important information remotely, although some advanced features work better on desktop. In terms of value for money, it can be worth the investment for medium-sized or expanding businesses that need more advanced accounting capabilities than basic bookkeeping software offers.
reviews.cons: The software can feel overwhelming for new users because of the large number of features and settings. There is definitely a learning curve in the beginning. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. The mobile version is useful for basic tasks but does not provide the full desktop experience.

reviews.cons: The interface can feel outdated and unintuitive at times, especially for new users. Some processes require multiple steps that could be streamlined, and performance can slow down with larger company files, which impacts overall efficiency.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: Powerful Accounting Software for Growing Businesses
reviews.name: Mailen G.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise has been a solid solution for managing accounting, invoicing, and business operations in one place. It offers powerful features for growing businesses, especially those that need advanced inventory tracking, detailed reporting, and multi-user access. While it has a learning curve at first, once everything is set up properly it becomes a very efficient system for daily operations. One of the biggest advantages of QuickBooks Enterprise is its robust invoicing and invoice management tools. Creating invoices is fast and customizable, and tracking payments is very straightforward. The reporting features are also excellent and provide valuable insights for financial management. The software handles large amounts of data smoothly compared to simpler accounting platforms. Customer support has generally been helpful when dealing with setup or technical questions, and there are many online resources and tutorials available. The mobile access is convenient for checking important information remotely, although some advanced features work better on desktop. In terms of value for money, it can be worth the investment for medium-sized or expanding businesses that need more advanced accounting capabilities than basic bookkeeping software offers.
reviews.cons: The software can feel overwhelming for new users because of the large number of features and settings. There is definitely a learning curve in the beginning. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. The mobile version is useful for basic tasks but does not provide the full desktop experience.

reviews.cons: The interface can feel outdated and unintuitive at times, especially for new users. Some processes require multiple steps that could be streamlined, and performance can slow down with larger company files, which impacts overall efficiency.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: Powerful Accounting Software for Growing Businesses
reviews.name: Mailen G.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise has been a solid solution for managing accounting, invoicing, and business operations in one place. It offers powerful features for growing businesses, especially those that need advanced inventory tracking, detailed reporting, and multi-user access. While it has a learning curve at first, once everything is set up properly it becomes a very efficient system for daily operations. One of the biggest advantages of QuickBooks Enterprise is its robust invoicing and invoice management tools. Creating invoices is fast and customizable, and tracking payments is very straightforward. The reporting features are also excellent and provide valuable insights for financial management. The software handles large amounts of data smoothly compared to simpler accounting platforms. Customer support has generally been helpful when dealing with setup or technical questions, and there are many online resources and tutorials available. The mobile access is convenient for checking important information remotely, although some advanced features work better on desktop. In terms of value for money, it can be worth the investment for medium-sized or expanding businesses that need more advanced accounting capabilities than basic bookkeeping software offers.
reviews.cons: The software can feel overwhelming for new users because of the large number of features and settings. There is definitely a learning curve in the beginning. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. The mobile version is useful for basic tasks but does not provide the full desktop experience.

reviews.cons: The interface can feel outdated and unintuitive at times, especially for new users. Some processes require multiple steps that could be streamlined, and performance can slow down with larger company files, which impacts overall efficiency.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise has been a solid solution for managing accounting, invoicing, and business operations in one place. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. The mobile version is useful for basic tasks but does not provide the full desktop experience.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

The reporting features are also excellent and provide valuable insights for financial management. The software handles large amounts of data smoothly compared to simpler accounting platforms. Customer support has generally been helpful when dealing with setup or technical questions, and there are many online resources and tutorials available. The mobile access is convenient for checking important information remotely, although some advanced features work better on desktop. In terms of value for money, it can be worth the investment for medium-sized or expanding businesses that need more advanced accounting capabilities than basic bookkeeping software offers.
reviews.cons: The software can feel overwhelming for new users because of the large number of features and settings. There is definitely a learning curve in the beginning. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. reviews.cons: It didn't have the capabilities of an ERP software that you can customize to your own specifications. It is good for a smaller company.

reviews.title: Quickbooks Is the Bomb!
reviews.name: Sherrie G.
reviews.pros: Invoicing, monthly reporting and financial activities, ease of use and time saving features that make my life easier
reviews.cons: Sometimes it's difficult to get to the right customer service area. I have been put on hold many times just to be transferred to various other departments.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.cons: Some challenges with updates, specifically switching to single use and locking out users inadvertently. Multiuser should really be the standard for enterprise.

reviews.cons: It didn't have the capabilities of an ERP software that you can customize to your own specifications. It is good for a smaller company.

reviews.cons: Sometimes it's difficult to get to the right customer service area. I have been put on hold many times just to be transferred to various other departments.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: Powerful Accounting Software for Growing Businesses
reviews.name: Mailen G.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise has been a solid solution for managing accounting, invoicing, and business operations in one place. It offers powerful features for growing businesses, especially those that need advanced inventory tracking, detailed reporting, and multi-user access. While it has a learning curve at first, once everything is set up properly it becomes a very efficient system for daily operations. One of the biggest advantages of QuickBooks Enterprise is its robust invoicing and invoice management tools. Creating invoices is fast and customizable, and tracking payments is very straightforward. The reporting features are also excellent and provide valuable insights for financial management. The software handles large amounts of data smoothly compared to simpler accounting platforms. Customer support has generally been helpful when dealing with setup or technical questions, and there are many online resources and tutorials available. The mobile access is convenient for checking important information remotely, although some advanced features work better on desktop. In terms of value for money, it can be worth the investment for medium-sized or expanding businesses that need more advanced accounting capabilities than basic bookkeeping software offers.
reviews.cons: The software can feel overwhelming for new users because of the large number of features and settings. There is definitely a learning curve in the beginning. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. The mobile version is useful for basic tasks but does not provide the full desktop experience.

reviews.cons: The desktop-based architecture feels outdated compared to modern cloud ERP systems Integration with non-Intuit third-party tools is limited and sometimes buggy Customization options are not as flexible as cloud-based ERPs like Odoo or NetSuite Performance may lag with large data files or when accessed over network

reviews.pros: Quickbooks really does what you need it to do. It is relatively easy to use (if you're OK with technology). It saves us SO much time. We do all our invoicing through QB. Their customer support is OK, but it is a good program at a good price. When there are bugs, they seem to be resolved quickly.
reviews.cons: I have noticed that they do a lot of updates. The most recent one changed everything around, which is fine, but I know some people have a hard time finding things. I also feel like they don't have enough information online, or it is really out of date. I feel like some customer service representatives don't understand the program.

reviews.title: Accounting Manager
reviews.name: Jeanne S.
reviews.pros: The inventory system is easy to use. We spent less time on training new employees because it was so user friendly and intuitive. I recently left the company where i used QB's Enterprise inventory and went to a new office that uses and ERP . The ERP isn't intuitive for staff and take a lot longer to learn how to use it.
reviews.cons: It didn't have the capabilities of an ERP software that you can customize to your own specifications. It is good for a smaller company.

reviews.title: Quickbooks Is the Bomb!
reviews.name: Sherrie G.
reviews.pros: Invoicing, monthly reporting and financial activities, ease of use and time saving features that make my life easier
reviews.cons: Sometimes it's difficult to get to the right customer service area. I have been put on hold many times just to be transferred to various other departments.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: Powerful Accounting Software for Growing Businesses
reviews.name: Mailen G.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise has been a solid solution for managing accounting, invoicing, and business operations in one place. It offers powerful features for growing businesses, especially those that need advanced inventory tracking, detailed reporting, and multi-user access. The reporting features are also excellent and provide valuable insights for financial management. The software handles large amounts of data smoothly compared to simpler accounting platforms. Customer support has generally been helpful when dealing with setup or technical questions, and there are many online resources and tutorials available. The mobile access is convenient for checking important information remotely, although some advanced features work better on desktop. In terms of value for money, it can be worth the investment for medium-sized or expanding businesses that need more advanced accounting capabilities than basic bookkeeping software offers.
reviews.cons: The software can feel overwhelming for new users because of the large number of features and settings. There is definitely a learning curve in the beginning. Occasionally there are bugs or performance slowdowns, especially after updates or when working with large company files. The mobile version is useful for basic tasks but does not provide the full desktop experience.

reviews.cons: The desktop-based architecture feels outdated compared to modern cloud ERP systems Integration with non-Intuit third-party tools is limited and sometimes buggy Customization options are not as flexible as cloud-based ERPs like Odoo or NetSuite Performance may lag with large data files or when accessed over network

reviews.name: Cayla F.
reviews.pros: Quickbooks really does what you need it to do. It is relatively easy to use (if you're OK with technology). It saves us SO much time. We do all our invoicing through QB. Their customer support is OK, but it is a good program at a good price. When there are bugs, they seem to be resolved quickly.
reviews.cons: I have noticed that they do a lot of updates. The most recent one changed everything around, which is fine, but I know some people have a hard time finding things. I also feel like they don't have enough information online, or it is really out of date. I feel like some customer service representatives don't understand the program.

reviews.title: Accounting Manager
reviews.name: Jeanne S.
reviews.pros: The inventory system is easy to use. We spent less time on training new employees because it was so user friendly and intuitive. I recently left the company where i used QB's Enterprise inventory and went to a new office that uses and ERP . The ERP isn't intuitive for staff and take a lot longer to learn how to use it.
reviews.cons: It didn't have the capabilities of an ERP software that you can customize to your own specifications. It is good for a smaller company.

reviews.title: Quickbooks Is the Bomb!
reviews.name: Sherrie G.
reviews.pros: Invoicing, monthly reporting and financial activities, ease of use and time saving features that make my life easier
reviews.cons: Sometimes it's difficult to get to the right customer service area. I have been put on hold many times just to be transferred to various other departments.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.

reviews.title: QuickBooks Enterprise
reviews.name: Terry C.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Enterprise is a very large program with the capability to support multiple lists and items. For someone who would like to utilize historical data across the platform, it is excellent. The interface of the program acts like many other software products and is not "accountant-ease" but rather English based so seems more logical for a user who is not familiar with accounting software. Invoicing, receiving payments and managing inventory are are very good in the software.
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Enterprise is not without it's problems. As lists grow the speed of the system will become slower. Customer Service is also sometimes a problems. I am a former Pro-Advisor for Intuit and remember a time when their Customer Service was outstanding. In prior years, we used to have a dedicated representative that would follow the problem until it was resolved. Today, the outsourcing of service has made that impossible which makes it difficult if not cumbersome to work a problem through to resolution without needing to explain everything over. Also, at one time you could purchase the software outright. Today it is subscription based per year. The rising cost of the subscription is becoming prohibitive on an annual basis.

reviews.title: The Best Program Ever!!
reviews.name: Natalie Y.
reviews.pros: I absolutely love QuickBooks, it is so easy to navigate. I like how it keeps track of all the data from invoices to customers and employees. This program has been a life saver to our little business.
reviews.cons: I don’t really have a negative to say besides when calling customer service support you can plan to be o the phone for a bit.

reviews.title: Still the best accounting software
reviews.name: James M.
reviews.pros: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise offers a significant performance advantage over QuickBooks Online. Its speed and efficiency are critical to my workflow. I have relied on QuickBooks Desktop since the 1990s and it has consistently met my business needs. The comprehensive functionality of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise supports essential accounting processes, including payroll management, credit card processing, bank transaction downloads, multi-company file management, employee access to pay stubs and W-2s, budgeting, forecasting, and payroll tax payments. The ability to simultaneously manage multiple company files is particularly valuable, and I would welcome future enhancements that increase this capacity. The current disparity in processing time between QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise and QuickBooks Online is substantial; tasks completed in one hour within the desktop environment require approximately four hours in the online version. A mandated transition to QuickBooks Online would severely impact my productivity and potentially necessitate a reevaluation of my career path. In summary, QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise remains a superior solution for my accounting needs. Its robust feature set and performance are unmatched, and any transition to a less efficient platform would be detrimental."
reviews.cons: QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise exhibits a persistent limitation when processing bulk form transmissions. Specifically, the system consistently generates errors when attempting to send more than 120 forms concurrently. For organizations with high-volume invoicing, such as ours, this translates to a significant operational inefficiency. For example, processing 400 invoices necessitates sending the initial 125, followed by manually queuing the remaining 275 invoices via the 'Send Later' function. This requires 275 individual mouse clicks, representing a substantial time investment. This issue has persisted for an extended period, spanning approximately two decades, without resolution. Furthermore, the current pricing structure of QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise presents a substantial financial burden. The discontinuation of QuickBooks Pro, previously available at a more accessible price point (approximately $199), and the mandatory adoption of the Enterprise subscription model have resulted in a significant cost increase. In 2024, our five-user license cost $4,579. Transitioning to a single-user license in 2025 resulted in a cost of $1,711. Compounding this, the shift from perpetual licenses to annual subscriptions has drastically increased the total cost of ownership. A software investment that previously yielded a multi-year lifespan now necessitates annual renewals, effectively increasing the five-year expenditure from the original $1,700 to $8,500. This pricing model represents a considerable financial commitment and warrants reevaluation.
